newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Thai refiners cutting runs on poor margins - PTT.
newsitem.headline: Thai refiners cutting runs on poor margins - PTT.

text.p: Thai refineries are being forced to cut runs due to weak refining profits, Adul Leelapatranurak, executive director of Petroleum Authority of Thailand's (PTT) refining sector group said on Wednesday.

"Refiners have to optimise. If they cannot sell their products, they have to cut throughputs," Leelapatranurak, a speaker at a conference on the economics of managing downstream operations, told Reuters.
He said refining margins were poor, possibly as low as $4 a barrel but refiners needed at least $5-$6 to break even.
"I think the cut is very small, about less than 10 percent," he confirmed but he said he did not have specific details of how specific refineries were operating.
PTT has shares in four of Thailand's five refineries, which have a combioned capacity of 760,000 barresl per day (bpd).
Refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc said in September it cut runs for five days at its 120,000 barrel-per-day (bpd) refinery by 20,000 bpd.
Rayong refinery cuts its 145,000 bpd production to 130,000 bpd mid September.
